findings: Every concrete digest interface in this file supplies a copy function. Earlier NULL-copy allocation concern is a defensive branch concern, not a demonstrated reachable leak for this interface table.

External digest update overwrites rather than streams, accepts unvalidated character arithmetic, truncates odd nibble and stores half input length into guint8. Callers must constrain syntax and length; reachability not checked.
Cumulative digest uses XOR into a4-to64-byte state whose length is chosen by first update. This is specialized aggregation, not exact ordered file-content proof.
GLib, SHA3 and BLAKE extraction wrappers copy state before finalization; XXH3 and Highway use non-destructive output APIs. This describes wrapper intent, not external algorithm verification.
BLAKE2 state initialization/update/finalization status codes are ignored in adapters; fixed configured output lengths constrain normal calls.
SSE toggle checks runtime sse4.2 when compiled with feature detection. No portable speedup is inferred from availability.
